web.markdown:
For AI agents: the docs index is at https://telegram-bot-sdk.readme.io/llms.txt. Append .md to any documentation page URL to get its markdown version.

| Time | Status | User Agent |  |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Make a request to see history. |

#### URL Expired

The URL for this request expired after 30 days.

Use this method to specify a URL and receive incoming updates via an outgoing webhook. Whenever there is an update for the bot, we will send an HTTPS POST request to the specified URL, containing a JSON-serialized [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update). In case of an unsuccessful request, we will give up after a reasonable amount of attempts.

If you'd like to make sure that the Webhook request comes from Telegram, we recommend using a secret path in the URL, e.g. `https://www.example.com/{token}`. Since nobody else knows your bot‘s token, you can be pretty sure it’s us.

See [setWebhook](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#setwebhook) official docs for a list of supported parameters and other info.

> ## 📘  Notes
>
> **1.** You will not be able to receive updates using [getUpdates](https://telegram-bot-sdk.readme.io/docs/getupdates) for as long as an outgoing webhook is set up.
>
> **2.** To use a self-signed certificate, you need to upload your [public key certificate](https://core.telegram.org/bots/self-signed) using the certificate parameter. Please upload as InputFile, sending a String will not work.
>
> **3.** Ports currently supported for Webhooks: **443**, **80**, **88**, **8443**.

Upload your public key certificate so that the root certificate in use can be checked. See our self-signed guide [https://core.telegram.org/bots/self-signed](https://core.telegram.org/bots/self-signed) for details.

web.title: How to set Telegram bot webhook?
web.description:
# Set Webhook
```http
Use with AI
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot{my_bot_token}/setWebhook?url={url_to_send_updates_to}
```

```http
Use with AI
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11/setWebhook?url=https://www.example.com
```

# Delete Webhook
```http
Use with AI
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot{my_bot_token}/setWebhook?url=
```

# Get Webhook
```http
Use with AI
GET https://api.telegram.org/bot{my_bot_token}/getWebhookInfo
```

## 2 Comments
You can **set Telegram bot webhook in command line** using npm package `sethook` and `npx` without installation.

## Set Webhook:
```bash
Use with AICopy
npx sethook <telegram_bot_token> <url>
```

## Delete Webhook:
```bash
Use with AICopy
npx sethook <telegram_bot_token>
```

# setWebhook [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html\#setwebhook "Link to this heading")

Returns: `bool`

_class_ aiogram.methods.set\_webhook.SetWebhook( _\*_, _url:str_, _certificate:[InputFile](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/types/input_file.html#aiogram.types.input_file.InputFile "aiogram.types.input_file.InputFile") \|None=None_, _ip\_address:str\|None=None_, _max\_connections:int\|None=None_, _allowed\_updates:list\[str\]\|None=None_, _drop\_pending\_updates:bool\|None=None_, _secret\_token:str\|None=None_, _\*\*extra\_data:Any_) [\[source\]](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/_modules/aiogram/methods/set_webhook.html#SetWebhook) [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook "Link to this definition")

Use this method to specify a URL and receive incoming updates via an outgoing webhook. Whenever there is an update for the bot, we will send an HTTPS POST request to the specified URL, containing a JSON-serialized [`aiogram.types.update.Update`](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/types/update.html#aiogram.types.update.Update "aiogram.types.update.Update"). In case of an unsuccessful request, we will give up after a reasonable amount of attempts. Returns `True` on success.
If you’d like to make sure that the webhook was set by you, you can specify secret data in the parameter _secret\_token_. If specified, the request will contain a header ‘X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token’ with the secret token as content.

> **Notes**
>
> **1.** You will not be able to receive updates using [`aiogram.methods.get_updates.GetUpdates`](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/get_updates.html#aiogram.methods.get_updates.GetUpdates "aiogram.methods.get_updates.GetUpdates") for as long as an outgoing webhook is set up.
>
> **2.** To use a self-signed certificate, you need to upload your [public key certificate](https://core.telegram.org/bots/self-signed) using _certificate_ parameter. Please upload as InputFile, sending a String will not work.
>
> **3.** Ports currently supported _for webhooks_: **443, 80, 88, 8443**.
> If you’re having any trouble setting up webhooks, please check out this [amazing guide to webhooks](https://core.telegram.org/bots/webhooks).

Source: [https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#setwebhook](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#setwebhook)

url _:str_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.url "Link to this definition")

HTTPS URL to send updates to. Use an empty string to remove webhook integration

certificate _: [InputFile](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/types/input_file.html#aiogram.types.input_file.InputFile "aiogram.types.input_file.InputFile") \|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.certificate "Link to this definition")

Upload your public key certificate so that the root certificate in use can be checked. See our [self-signed guide](https://core.telegram.org/bots/self-signed) for details.

ip\_address _:str\|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.ip_address "Link to this definition")

The fixed IP address which will be used to send webhook requests instead of the IP address resolved through DNS

max\_connections _:int\|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.max_connections "Link to this definition")

The maximum allowed number of simultaneous HTTPS connections to the webhook for update delivery, 1-100. Defaults to _40_. Use lower values to limit the load on your bot’s server, and higher values to increase your bot’s throughput.

allowed\_updates _:list\[str\]\|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.allowed_updates "Link to this definition")

A JSON-serialized list of the update types you want your bot to receive. For example, specify `["message", "edited_channel_post", "callback_query"]` to only receive updates of these types. See [`aiogram.types.update.Update`](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/types/update.html#aiogram.types.update.Update "aiogram.types.update.Update") for a complete list of available update types. Specify an empty list to receive all update types except _chat\_member_, _message\_reaction_, and _message\_reaction\_count_ (default). If not specified, the previous setting will be used.

drop\_pending\_updates _:bool\|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.drop_pending_updates "Link to this definition")

Pass `True` to drop all pending updates

secret\_token _:str\|None_ [¶](https://docs.aiogram.dev/en/v3.16.0/api/methods/set_webhook.html#aiogram.methods.set_webhook.SetWebhook.secret_token "Link to this definition")

A secret token to be sent in a header ‘X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token’ in every webhook request, 1-256 characters. Only characters `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-` are allowed. The header is useful to ensure that the request comes from a webhook set by you.
